title: AI Stocks Are Crashing. Here’s What I’m Actually Doing
creator: Couch Investor
summary: Couch Investor argues the AI sell-off is headline-driven: stocks outran their businesses and valuations are catching up, but the large names' businesses are still growing fast, so he says he will stick with what he has rather than make a new buy list. Amazon is the most positive name discussed: AWS grew 39.3% year on year to about $46 billion, with a $578 billion backlog, and he calls it extremely cheap and a buy-and-hold name, though no formal new call is recorded. Reddit beat earnings but user metrics missed and logged-out traffic is falling; he puts it to the side, keeps a small position, and would probably buy more only if external data shows traffic increasing, recorded as UNCERTAIN rather than a firm call. Intel missed its fourth-quarter guide, with the foundry the swing factor; the stock is down 51% from its peak but still up 75% year to date. He also says he is thinking of selling completely out of Rubrik because its valuation does not make sense against cheaper names, stated as a consideration rather than an action, so it is recorded as UNCERTAIN, not a firm SELL. No other firm new call is made.
